myunbin opened PR #14896 from myunbin:add-rules-261021 to bytecodealliance:main:

Add mid-end optimization rules:

  • (~x | y) ^ x --> ~(x & y)
  • (~x OP y) ^ (~y OP x) --> x ^ y, where OP = {&, |}
  • (~x | y) & (~y | x) --> ~(x ^ y)
  • max(x, y) OP min(x, y) --> x OP y, where OP = {&, |, ^}
  • max(~x, ~y) --> ~min(x, y)
  • min(~x, ~y) --> ~max(x, y)
  • ~max(~x, y) --> min(x, ~y)
  • ~min(~x, y) --> max(x, ~y)
  • -(x & y) + x --> x & ~y
  • (~x & y) + (~y & x) --> x ^ y
  • (-x) - (~x) --> 1
  • ~x + C --> (C - 1) - x
  • (x + C) ^ -1 --> (-(C + 1)) - x
  • (x | C) - C --> x & ~C
  • (x | C) ^ (y | C) --> (x ^ y) & ~C
  • (x | C) ^ (y ^ C) --> (x & ~C) ^ y
  • (x << 1) * C --> x * (2 * C)
  • ~rotl(~x, k) --> rotl(x, k)
  • ~rotr(~x, k) --> rotr(x, k)
  • (x << 1) == x --> x == 0
  • (x >>u 1) == x --> x == 0
  • (~x & y) == y --> (x & y) == 0
  • ~x == (~x | y) --> (x & y) == 0
  • umax(x, y) OP 0 --> (x | y) OP 0, where OP = {==, !=}
  • umax(x, y) OP umin(x, y) --> x OP y, where OP = {==, !=}
  • (x >=s y) & (y >=s x) --> x == y
  • (x >=u y) & (y >=u x) --> x == y
  • select(c, x, y) == select(c, y, x) --> x == y
  • select(x == 0, -x, x) --> x, and corresponding x != 0
  • select(x == 0, 0, x OP y) --> x OP y, where OP = {&, *}, and corresponding x != 0
  • ~select(c, C1, C2) --> select(c, ~C1, ~C2)
  • -select(c, C1, C2) --> select(c, -C1, -C2)

Thanks!

:thumbs_up: cfallin submitted PR review:

Thanks! The new rules look good generally. Just one question below about a possible pessimization.

:speech_balloon: cfallin created PR review comment:

This seems like a regression -- we won't use the native negation instruction anymore but instead will load a zero-constant and do a subtract. Could you look into what's going on here (cost function discrepancies or something else)?
:memo: myunbin submitted PR review.

:speech_balloon: myunbin created PR review comment:

@cfallin

I believe it's because of the rule ~x + C → (C - 1) - x.

When C=1, both rules match:

  • ~x + 1 → (1 - 1) - x → 0 - x (added rule in this pr)
  • ~x + 1 → -x (existing one)

The cost model assigns both candidates as 4: ineg(4) and iconst(1) - isub(3), therefore tie.
Maybe the tie breaker chooses 0 - x afterward.
:speech_balloon: myunbin edited PR review comment.
:speech_balloon: myunbin edited PR review comment.
:speech_balloon: myunbin edited PR review comment.
:memo: cfallin submitted PR review.

:speech_balloon: cfallin created PR review comment:

Interesting. Probably we should adjust the cost of ineg: on all CPUs I'm aware of, a unary integer negation operator has the same cost as other ALU ops (1 cycle) so it should win against a const materialization plus an ALU op. Can you bundle that change in here and see if it fixes this regression?
myunbin updated PR #14896.
:memo: myunbin submitted PR review.

:speech_balloon: myunbin created PR review comment:

I adjusted ineg to have same cost with other ALU ops. I guess all affected test cases now produce ineg.
:speech_balloon: myunbin edited PR review comment.

cfallin commented on PR #14896:

@myunbin it looks like there is a verifier failure now -- could you take a look?

myunbin commented on PR #14896:

@cfallin I found two issues while investigating this failure.

  1. iconst_u spec seems to treat the result as a single integer rather than a splat. For example, the verifier reports: iconst_u({bits: 32, lanes: 4}, 1) -> [1, 0, 0, 0]. A splat would produce [1, 1, 1, 1]. The spec seems to be missing the per-lane semantics for supported vector types. I can investigate more and open a separate PR.

<details>
<summary>log</summary>

isub({bits: 32, lanes: 4}, [#x00 #x00 #x00 #x00], [#xff #xff #xff #xff]) -> [#x01 #x01 #x01
#x01]
ineg({bits: 32, lanes: 4}, [#x00 #x00 #x00 #x00]) -> [#x00 #x00 #x00 #x00]
bnot({bits: 32, lanes: 4}, [#x00 #x00 #x00 #x00]) -> [#xff #xff #xff #xff]
iconst_u({bits: 32, lanes: 4}, #x0000000000000001) -> [#x01 #x00 #x00 #x00]
simplify([#x01 #x01 #x01 #x01]) -> [#x01 #x00 #x00 #x00]
violated: cranelift/codegen/src/spec/opt.isle line 71: e123
violated: cranelift/codegen/src/spec/opt.isle line 20: e167

</details>

  1. I guess rule (rule (simplify (isub ty (ineg ty x) (bnot ty x))) (iconst_u ty 1)) crashes. Currently iconst_u only supports scalar and vec128, but this rule can also match other vector widths, causing a panic. I'll restrict the rule to the supported types for now. Is there a reason the helper's vector support is limited to 128 bits?
